properties.name: MemoryBackend moves HashMap → BTreeMap; export build 1,137ms → 236ms
properties.rationale:
⚖️ THE TRADE IS REAL AND WAS PUT IN THE COMMIT RATHER THAN OMITTED. `BTreeMap` insert is O(log n) where `HashMap` was O(1), and import measured 890.6 ms -> 966.8 ms, about 8% SLOWER. It is worth it on the round trip — a session's load+save goes 2,266 ms -> 1,421 ms, 37% better — but a report carrying only the 4.8x would have been selecting the evidence.

🛑 SCOPE, WHICH MATTERS AND IS EASY TO OVERSTATE: THIS DOES NOT MAKE TODAY'S REFLOW2 FASTER. Production runs on RocksDB, whose prefix iterator is already a range scan. What it speeds up is (a) the 1,452-test core suite, which runs entirely on `MemoryBackend`, and (b) the database-free session model under discussion in `dec:idea-does-reflow2-need-a-byte-store-at-all-or-only-durability`, where the memory backend IS the store.

⭐⭐ THIRD DEFECT OF ONE SHAPE IN ONE FILE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING — not three coincidences. A linear scan standing in where an indexed lookup belongs: twice in the write buffer (#330 — the buffered `get`, and the `prefix_scan` pre-flight) and once here in the backing store. All three were invisible at test scale and quadratic at design scale, because the cost is a product of two things that are both small in a unit test and both large in a real design.

⭐ AND ALL THREE WERE FOUND THE SAME WAY: read the code, count the operations, check the arithmetic against the stopwatch BEFORE changing anything. 42M comparisons at ~25 ns predicts ~1.06 s against 1,137 ms measured. The method is transferable and the habit is the transferable part — the first hypothesis in #330 was wrong (adjacency read-modify-write) and reading the code killed it before any code was written.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
Merged as #331. `MemoryBackend` held each column family in a `HashMap`, but `KvBackend` requires ORDERED prefix iteration — so `prefix_scan` iterated the whole column family, filtered by prefix, and sorted the result: O(n log n) per scan, on the backend whose entire purpose is to be the fast path. `export_graph` calls `outgoing()` once per node, so exporting reflow2's own design was 3,149 scans over a 13,414-entry adjacency map, ~42M key comparisons.

Six `BTreeMap`s now, and `prefix_scan` is a range query — seek to the prefix, take while it matches. `BTreeMap` orders keys lexicographically, the same order RocksDB's default byte-wise comparator gives, so the trait's ordered-scan contract is satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION and the sort was deleted rather than optimised.

MEASURED (release, in-memory backend, fulltext on, 3,149 nodes / 13,414 edges):

    build export doc   1,137.3 ms -> 236.5 ms   (4.8x)
    serialize to JSON     31.0 ms ->  28.8 ms
    TOTAL session save 1,168.3 ms -> 265.3 ms   (4.4x)

Workspace 1760 / 0, core 1452 / 0, both clippy gates, fmt, twelve python gates and the design gate green; CI green on both jobs.
